analysis.title: Oil's next shockwave: oil explodes, bonds scream recession and Europe is the sucker
key_insights: Oil is accelerating toward $120 after its latest breakout. The $118 level is the highest close since the oil turmoil began and remains an important hurdle.
Oil volatility is picking up after being largely absent during the squeeze. The Market Ear's view is to use upside optionality to express a bullish oil view or to hedge against further upside risk.
CTAs have been buying oil recently, but positioning is far from extreme long levels. With momentum accelerating, there is room for more systematic buying.

Oil and the US 10-year yield moved closely together until the latest collapse in yields. The short-term divergence is now extreme. Oil is pricing persistent inflationary pressure, while bonds are pricing weaker growth and flight-to-quality demand.

French yields remain under upward pressure, unlike US Treasuries. Europe's energy vulnerability adds to an already fragile fiscal and political backdrop, though the French bond selloff has causes beyond oil.
The SX5E has moved in an almost perfect inverse relationship with oil and gas since the latest squeeze began, showing Europe's energy vulnerability in equity performance.
European banks, previously resilient, are now absorbing negative shocks from surging oil prices and rising French yields, and are starting to look like Europe's weak link.

sector_views.rationale: Banks are catching negative shocks from higher oil prices and rising French yields and are described as Europe's latest weak link.
